label: early original-phase input of 3/f/e/c/x/d, gated by sequence-start context
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t >= 1) & (t <= 4) & isin(in_tok, [tok("3"), tok("f"), tok("e"), tok("c"), tok("x"), tok("d")]) & isin(first_tok, [tok("a"),tok("r"),tok("o"),tok("n"),tok("i"),tok("g"),tok("k"),tok("l"),tok("h"),tok("f"),tok("x")])
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, essentially at positions t=1..5, peaking at t=2-3; never at t=0, the delimiter, or the copy phase. The current input is almost always one of 3, f, e, c, x, d (3 strongest, then f/e). Whether it fires depends graded-ly on the preceding prefix: sequences starting with a, r, o, n (and to a lesser degree i, g, k, l, h, f, x) and with prev tokens f/x/3/e/d/h strongly enable it; prefixes with tokens like s, t, u, v, w, b, q suppress it. Largest activations are 3/f/e at t=2-3 after prefixes like "a o", "a a 3", "r o f". Mostly fires on first occurrence of the input token. The prefix dependence looks like a weighted sum not captured by a clean set rule, so precision stays low (~0.3) while the predicate covers ~80% of activation mass.
